land.text: Cliopatria's Moghulistan shape of 1516, the Moghul lands west of the Tarim: 'western Moghulistan (the area of modern Kyrgyzstan)' and the Zhetysu, the part Cliopatria does not give to Eastern Moghulistan

predecessors.note: Cliopatria ends its Moghulistan row in 1518 and opens Eastern and Western Moghulistan in 1519 (943 cells here, 3,289 in the east).

land.text: the Tian Shan lands that 'were gradually lost to Kyrgyz tribes' (Moghulistan page)

successors.note: The Kyrgyz page has the Kyrgyz 'established a Kyrgyz khanate in 1514' (a reference note citing Williams 2020) and 'Various Turkic peoples ruled them until 1685, when they came under the control of the Oirats'. The Cliopatria rows after 1565 are not Moghul (verdict wrong); in Cliopatria the cells go to its Oirat Confederation shape in 1636. There is no Kyrgyz Khanate dossier yet (suggested slug kyrgyz-khanate).

capitals.name: Almaliq (Huocheng)
capitals.note: Weak: the Moghulistan page's infobox gives only 'Capital: Almaliq' (no dates, the 14th-15th century khanate). No page opened names a seat for western Moghulistan after 1503, when Tashkent (Mahmud Khan's seat) was seized by the Uzbeks; Almaliq is the khanate's capital of record. Reviewer (2026-10-19): ended in 1520, because Almaliq (80.88 E, 44.2 N) lies in the Zhetysu cells lost to the Kazakhs in 1521 (/ledger/1) and outside every Western Moghulistan shape from 1521 (bbox north edge 42.89 N in shapes.csv); no page names a seat for 1521-1565.

keyframe_review.note: 285,072 km2 for 1519-20 (943 cells; 73.4-81.1 E, 38.5-46.5 N): Zhetysu and the Tian Shan. The Moghulistan page calls Mahmud Khan (1487-1508) 'the ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent' but also says 'The rest of western Moghulistan (the area of modern Kyrgyzstan) were gradually lost to Kyrgyz tribes' and that the Kyrgyz 'by 1510-11 ... had effectively driven out the Moghuls', so the Moghul hold on the south of this shape is doubtful. No page opened gives an outline or an infobox area; the shape stands as the Moghul claim, soft.

140,441 km2 for 1521-25 (468 cells; 73.4-80.2 E, 38.5-42.9 N, the Tian Shan between Issyk-Kul and the Tarim): the 1519 outline without the 475 Zhetysu cells that Cliopatria gives to its Kazakh Khanate shape of 1521 (the kazakh-khanate dossier records the 474-cell gain). Same caveat as 1519: the Kyrgyz page and the Moghulistan page put these mountains in Kyrgyz hands after 1510-11.

140,488 km2 for 1526-46: the 1521 outline unchanged. 'as late as 1526-27, the Moghul Khan Sultan Said still attempted but failed to return the Kyrgyz to subjugation' (Moghulistan page): an attempt to recover the Tian Shan that failed, so the Moghul claim here is nominal. Soft.

140,438 km2 for 1547-94: the shape is unchanged but should end in 1565. Abdurashid Khan (1533-1565 on the Moghulistan page; 'Reign: 1533 - 1560' on his own page) 'fought for control of (western) Moghulistan against the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde', and 'thereafter the Moghuls were largely restricted to possession of the Tarim Basin' (Moghulistan page). The Kazakh Khanate page still has Haqnazar 'defeated by the Oirats and the Moghuls in the 1560's when Haqnazar attempted to capture Jeitsu'.

correction.text: empty: no Moghul state in the Tian Shan after 1565; draw the land as Kyrgyz tribal land (kyrgyz-khanate once it has a dossier), otherwise nobody's

keyframe_review.note: 140,606 km2 for 1595-1608: no page opened shows a Moghul state in the Tian Shan after Abdurashid: 'thereafter the Moghuls were largely restricted to possession of the Tarim Basin' (Moghulistan page), the Kyrgyz page has Kyrgyz rule until 1685 and the Dzungar Khanate page has 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them'. Draw nothing as Western Moghulistan; the land is Kyrgyz (kyrgyz-khanate, no dossier yet).

correction.text: empty: no Moghul state in the Tian Shan after 1565; Kyrgyz land under Oirat pressure from 1609

keyframe_review.note: 140,438 km2 for 1609-31: as for 1595. The Dzungar Khanate page: 'From 1609-1616, the Oirats devastated the Kazakhs and the Kyrgyz, subjugating them in the process.'

correction.text: empty: no Moghul state in the Tian Shan after 1565; the land is Kyrgyz, with the Oirats from 1609 (Dzungar Khanate page) or 1685 (Kyrgyz page)

keyframe_review.note: 140,438 km2 for 1632-35: as for 1595. Cliopatria moves 467 of its 468 cells to its Oirat Confederation shape in 1636; the Kyrgyz page has 'Various Turkic peoples ruled them until 1685, when they came under the control of the Oirats', which dates the Oirat rule 49 years later than Cliopatria. Neither page names a Moghul state here.

region.text: western Moghulistan (the area of modern Kyrgyzstan) with the Zhetysu

ledger.note: 1519: Cliopatria opens Western Moghulistan, the Moghul lands of Zhetysu and the Tian Shan, when its Moghulistan row ends. The Moghulistan page dates no founding in 1519: it has Mahmud Khan (1487-1508) as 'the ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent', 'The brothers were defeated and captured; they were released but Tashkent was seized by the Uzbeks' (1503) and 'The rest of western Moghulistan (the area of modern Kyrgyzstan) were gradually lost to Kyrgyz tribes'. The year and the outline are Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Zhetysu part of the 1519 shape that the Kazakh Khanate shape of 1521 takes

ledger.note: 1521: the Kazakhs take Zhetysu. Cliopatria drops 475 cells here and the Kazakh Khanate shape of 1521 gains 474 of them. The Kazakh Khanate page does not date the loss: it has Qasim 'became the khan in 1511 and from that point only the descendants of Janibek Khan ruled Kazakh khanate' and shows the 'Territory of the Kazakh Khanate in the beginning of 16th century'. Confidence 1: year and land are Cliopatria's.

region.text: western Moghulistan, fought for against the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde

ledger.note: 1533: Abdurashid Khan begins the struggle for western Moghulistan. The Moghulistan page: Abdurashid Khan (1533-1565) 'also fought for control of (western) Moghulistan against the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde'. The page gives the reign, not a first battle; the kazakh-khanate dossier opens its contest in the same year. Zhetysu is my reading of the zone.

1565: the struggle ends with Abdurashid's reign. 'he was succeeded by Abdurashid Khan (1533-1565)' and 'thereafter the Moghuls were largely restricted to possession of the Tarim Basin'. The Abdurashid Khan page gives 'Reign: 1533 - 1560' and Abdul Karim at Yarkand 1560-1591; no page names a last battle or treaty.

region.text: western Moghulistan: the Zhetysu remnant and the Tian Shan

ledger.note: 1565: the Moghuls are 'largely restricted to possession of the Tarim Basin' and western Moghulistan ends. Year from the page's end of Abdurashid's reign; Cliopatria keeps the row to 1635 and no page opened shows a Moghul state in the Tian Shan after 1565 (the Kyrgyz page has Kyrgyz rule there until 1685).

wars.name: Kyrgyz revolt against the Moghuls

zones.text: western Moghulistan, 'the area of modern Kyrgyzstan'

wars.outcome: The Kyrgyz tribes, led by Tagai Biy, rebelled against the Moghuls and 'by 1510-11 ... had effectively driven out the Moghuls'; Sultan Said's attempt in 1526-27 to return them to subjugation failed.
wars.note: The Kyrgyz had migrated into the Tian Shan in 1469-70 (Moghulistan page); the first year of the revolt is not given, so 1510 is the page's 'effectively driven out'. Reviewer (2026-10-19): 'from' set to 1519, the start of this state; the revolt began under the predecessor moghulistan ('by 1510-11, they had effectively driven out the Moghuls', Moghulistan page).

wars.name: Abdurashid Khan's struggle with the Kazakhs for western Moghulistan
wars.outcome: No decisive result is given: Abdurashid 'fought for control of (western) Moghulistan against the Kirghiz-Kazakhs of the Great Horde' and afterwards the Moghuls were 'largely restricted to possession of the Tarim Basin'.
wars.note: The Kazakh Khanate page has Haqnazar 'defeated by the Oirats and the Moghuls in the 1560's when Haqnazar attempted to capture Jeitsu'.

certainty.note: A claim over mountain and steppe country whose frontiers no page opened describes; the Kyrgyz held much of it after 1510-11.

sources.title: Moghulistan
sources.note: Western Moghulistan under Mahmud Khan, the Kyrgyz expulsion of the Moghuls by 1510-11, Abdurashid's fight with the Kirghiz-Kazakhs 1533-1565, 'largely restricted to the Tarim Basin'.

sources.title: Kazakh Khanate
sources.note: Qasim Khan 1511, the 1560s defeat of Haqnazar by the Oirats and Moghuls in Jetisu, the Kazakh territory of the early 16th century.

sources.title: Kyrgyz people
sources.note: Kyrgyz khanate of 1514 (note), Kyrgyz rule until 1685 and Oirat control; the page is thin for 1450-1700.

sources.title: Abdurashid Khan
sources.note: Reign 1533-1560, succession of Abdul Karim in Yarkand in 1560; thin on western Moghulistan.

sources.title: Dzungar Khanate
sources.note: 1609-1616 Oirat subjugation of the Kazakhs and Kyrgyz, 1683-1685 Galdan's Kyrgyz campaigns, Jetisu held until 1745.

notes: Cliopatria's Western Moghulistan (1519-1635) is the Zhetysu and Tian Shan half of the old Moghulistan row; Eastern Moghulistan (the Tarim, the Yarkent Khanate) is the other half and is its own dossier. Not merged: the Moghulistan page has the Moghul realm split between Turpan (Ahmad Alaq, Mansur), Tashkent (Mahmud) and Kashgar (Said), and the two rows tile. Hard to support: no page opened shows a Moghul state in the Tian Shan after about 1514. The Moghulistan page has the Kyrgyz 'by 1510-11 ... effectively driven out the Moghuls' and Moghul rule 'largely restricted to ... the Tarim Basin' after 1565; the Kyrgyz page has Kyrgyz rule until the Oirats in 1685 and a Kyrgyz khanate of 1514 (a reference note). So the dossier lives 1519-1565, carries the Cliopatria shapes 1519-1565 as a soft Moghul claim, and marks the shapes of 1595-1635 wrong (empty correction = draw nothing as Western Moghulistan). Counterpart needing a dossier: a Kyrgyz khanate or Kyrgyz tribal lands (suggested slug kyrgyz-khanate, 1514-1685 on the Kyrgyz page), group ia-03-x. Cliopatria's 1636 transfer of 467 cells to its Oirat Confederation shape is outside this dossier's life; the Kyrgyz page puts the Oirat rule at 1685 and the Dzungar Khanate page at 1609-1616 and 1683-1685. Disagreements: Abdurashid's reign 1533-1565 (Moghulistan page, Kazakh dossier) against 1533-1560 (Abdurashid page); the Moghulistan page has 'in 1469-70 Kyrgyz belonging to the Oirat confederacy migrated into the Tian Shan' while the Kyrgyz page dates the Tian Shan migration to the 9th-10th century. No infobox area exists on any page opened. The Almaliq capital is a weak entry (see identity.capitals). Gazetteer: Semirechye exists; no 'Moghulistan' or 'Tian Shan' region (Kyrgyzstan used).
